artifact_status: Textured motion revision for user review; not runtime integrated.
method: Played the entire encoded continuity cut at 1x in the in-app browser. Inspected sampled browser frames and native approach, descent, recovery, contact and settled images. This is not a claim of continuous human inspection of every frame.
receipt_limits: Browser callback and decoded-frame counters have different baselines; ffprobe independently verifies all 288 encoded frames. No playback stalls or decoder errors were reported.
findings: Physical dock roofs, walls and ground use the preceding port's simpler slate/tan/concrete material treatment. The ship remains the detailed foreground subject.
Four larger battered areas read as fractured recessed metal with broken armor and emergency restraints. The scar textures remain attached in the sampled changed poses.
The ship advances left-to-right, descends with a bounded bank and bow dip, and returns level for support contact. The visible scene remains stationary.
Short white-blue lift effects remain at the nozzle mouths and stop after settlement. The inspected contact/end frames show no obvious floating supports or hull penetration.
limits: Motion remains authored rather than a dynamics simulation. The recovery is one slow asymmetric event, not violent uncontrolled tumbling.
Fixed-view generated surface projection retains baked shading and is not a complete multiangle texture atlas.
Finite geometry checks and sampled images cannot exclude every subframe collision or fine temporal artifact.
No audio or campaign runtime integration is included. Final creative acceptance remains with the user.
